shortDescription: The Coca-Cola Company NYSE:KO and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa to bottling partner Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF), marking a significant step in the beverage giant's efforts to streamline its operations while expanding its reach…

children: and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa to bottling partner Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF), marking a significant step in the beverage giant's efforts to streamline its operations while expanding its reach across emerging markets.

The transaction, valued at $2.6 billion when announced, allows Coca-Cola to reduce its direct exposure to capital-intensive bottling operations while maintaining its commercial relationship with a major regional partner.

Coca-Cola HBC manufactures, packages and distributes beverages across international markets. Unlike Coca-Cola, which focuses heavily on brand development and concentrate sales, its bottling partners manage much of the physical production and distribution.
The acquisition adds 14 African markets to Coca-Cola HBC's operations, making it the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottler by volume.
The expanded business now serves more than 1.2 billion consumers across 43 European and African markets.

For Coca-Cola, the deal reinforces a business strategy that prioritizes its high-margin concentrate operations while shifting manufacturing and distribution responsibilities to independent bottling partners.
Africa also presents a considerable long-term growth opportunity as beverage companies seek new customers beyond more mature Western markets.
Moreover, Coca-Cola retains a 25% stake in the African bottling business. A separate agreement allows Coca-Cola HBC to acquire that remaining interest within six years.
For Coca-Cola shareholders, the transaction's biggest appeal is the potential improvement in operating margins and capital efficiency.
Investors should monitor operating margins, free cash flow and organic revenue growth as Coca-Cola removes the African bottling operations from its consolidated financial results.
For Coca-Cola HBC, the acquisition is expected to boost earnings per share by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027 while keeping financial leverage within its target range of 1.5 to 2 times EBITDA.

The bottler's Feb. 17 earnings presentation will provide additional details about its African expansion strategy and integration plans. Currency fluctuations, regional inflation and integration expenses remain important risks.

title: Coca-Cola Completes Major $2.6 Billion Africa Deal
